questions.question: What are Guyots?

options.text: It is a flat topped seamount.
These are deep valleys, some comparable to the Grand Canyon.
It is a mountain with pointed summits.
These are low islands found in the tropical oceans consisting of coral reefs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a flat-topped seamount**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• These flat summits could be more than 10 kilometers in circumference.
 
• The Swiss-American geologist Arnold Henry Guyot is the source of the name.
 
• According to research, guyots are volcanic islands that form at the shallow crests of mid-oceanic ridges and rise.
 
• The islands are trimmed off by wave erosion both during and right after their development.
 
• The seafloor moves laterally away from ridge or rise crests at rates of several centimeters per year, according to the widely recognized idea of seafloor spreading.
 
• Guyots gradually plunge deeper as the seafloor spreads away from the crests and sinks at the same time.
 
• The majority of summits in the Pacific Ocean, where guyots are most prevalent, are between 1,000 and 2,000 meters below sea level.

questions.question: Which of the following energy resources is also known as Liquid Gold?

__

• Petroleum is commonly known as **Liquid gold.**
 
• Due to the fact that crude oil turns black when it is removed from the ground, petroleum is also known as "black gold."
 
• Petroleum is a liquid that naturally exists below the surface of the planet.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Natural gas** emits **fewer pollutants**, including sulfur dioxide (**SO2**), nitrogen oxides (**NOx**), **particulate matter**, and **greenhouse gases** such as carbon dioxide (**CO2**), compared to the other options listed. 
 
 
 
• **Coal:**
 
 
• Coal is a black or brown flammable substance found in sedimentary rocks.
 
• Coal is mainly composed of elements like carbon, hydrogen, sulfur, oxygen, and nitrogen.
 
 
 
• Uranium:
 
 
• ​It is a **silvery-white** metallic chemical element in the periodic table, with atomic number 92.

• Uranium has the highest **atomic weight (19 kg m**) of all naturally occurring elements.

questions.question: What type of compound is formed when one hydrogen atom in ammonia is substituted by an alkyl or aromatic group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary amine**__.

__
 
• **Primary Amine:** 

 
 
• Primary amines are formed when **one hydrogen atom** in **ammonia** is substituted by an **alkyl or aromatic group**.
 
• Some **examples** of primary alkyl amines include **amino acids** and **methylamine** while primary aromatic amines include **aniline**.
 
 
 
• **Secondary** **Amine:**
 
 
• Secondary amines are those amines that have **two organic substituents** either **alkyl** or **aryl ones or both**. They are bound to the nitrogen together with one hydrogen. A common example is **dimethylamine**. Likewise, diphenylamine is an example of an **aromatic amine**.
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d00360317628e577b6e85affad664506664b0c3369a52f9f3db4e1603f02c5c.png] 

 
Methyl isocyanide can be reduced to secondary amine in the presence of Lithium aluminum hydride (LiAIH4)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Carboxylic acid

 
 
• It is an organic compound containing a carboxyl functional group. They occur widely in nature and are produced synthetically. 
 
• The general formula of a carboxylic acid is R-COOH, where COOH refers to the carboxyl group and R refers to the rest of the molecule to which this carboxyl group is attached.
 
 
• In this case, there is a carbon that shares a double bond with an oxygen atom and a single bond with a hydroxyl group.
 
 
 
• The first four carboxylic acids derived from alkanes are - 
 
 
• Methanoic acid (Formic acid)
 
 
• 1 carbon
 
• HCOOH
 
 
 
• Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid or vinegar)
 
 
• 2 carbon
 
• CH3COOH
 
 
 
• Propanoic acid
 
 
• 3 carbon
 
• C2H5COOH
 
 
 
• Butanoic acid
 
 
• 4 carbon
 
• C3H7COOH
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ketone Body**:
 
 
• Ketone bodies are contained by the ketone group. 
 
• This **water-soluble compound** is produced in the **liver** during **caloric restrictions**.
 
• Ketone bodies act as an **energy source** in the **absence of glucose**.
 
• Ketone body when present in the liver is called **ketogenesis**.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with Atoll?

options.text: It is made up of two mountain chains separated by a large depression
Low islands found in the tropical oceans consisting of coral reefs
It is a seamount with a flat top
Ocean basins with gently sloping terrain

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef** surrounding a central lagoon. 
 
• Atolls are found in** tropical oceans** where the water is warm and clear.
 
• Coral reefs are made up of the skeletons of tiny marine organisms called **coral polyps**. 
 
• Coral polyps secrete a hard substance called **calcium carbonate** that forms the reef structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Mid-ocean ridge: **

 
 
• Mid-ocean ridges are mountain ranges that form at the divergent boundaries of tectonic plates. 
 
• As the plates move apart, magma from the Earth's mantle rises up and cools to form new oceanic crust.
 
 
 
• **Guyot: **
 
 
• Guyots are seamounts with flat tops that have been eroded by waves. 
 
• They are formed when a seamount erupts on the ocean floor and then subsides back into the water.
 
 
 
• **Abyssal plains:**
 
 
• Abyssal plains are the flattest and most common type of ocean floor. 
 
• They are formed by the deposition of sediment from land and from the erosion of seamounts and other underwater features.

questions.question: What does the ‘Print Range’ option allow you to do when printing a document?

options.text: Add header and footer information to the printed pages
Choose the specific pages or range of pages to be printed
Adjust the size of the printed document to fit on a specific number of pages
Print the document with different fonts and styles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Choose the specific pages or range of pages to be printed**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Print Range** option allows you to **specify which pages of a document** you want to print. 
 
• This is useful if you only need to print a few pages of a document, or if you want to print a specific section of a document.
 
• For example, if you have a 10-page document and you only want to print pages 5-7, you would use the Print Range option to specify pages 5-7. The printer would then only print pages 5-7 of the document.
 
• The Print Range option is typically available in the print settings dialog box of most printing applications. 
 
• The specific location of the option may vary depending on the application, but it is usually found in a section labeled "Pages" or "Print Range".

questions.question: Who among the following attacked Gujarat and plundered the Somnath Temple in the 11th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mahmud of Ghazni__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Somnath Temple** in **Gujarat** was attacked and plundered in the **11th century** by **Mahmud of Ghazni**.
 
• Specifically, this raid occurred in** 1025 **during one of **Mahmud's multiple invasions** of Indian kingdoms.
 
• His attack resulted in the destruction of the** jyotirlinga of the Somnath Temple**.
 
• This invasion is also known for the** punitive invasion of Anhilwara** that followed the **conquest of Somnath**.
 
• Notably, despite the destruction, there are records of **pilgrimages **to the temple in **1038** that do not mention damage, signifying potential repairs or rebuilds during this period.
 
• Indeed, the temple was later rebuilt, only to face destruction once again during **Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Gujarat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahmad Shah Abdali:**

 
 
• **​**Ahmad Shah Abdali also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani was imprisoned along with his brother Zulfikar in Shah Hussain Hotak's fortress in Old Kandahar in his early years.
 
• His numerous attacks led to the destruction of the Mughal Empire, creating a power vacuum.
 
• Abdali significantly impacted the northern Maratha's aspirations at Panipat through his consistent invasions, reflecting his tireless energy and ambition.
 
• His Afghan army emerged victorious from the battle after successfully destroying several Maratha flanks which led to a massive loss of between 60,000 and 70,000 troops.
 
 
 
• **Qutubuddin Aibak:**
 
 
• **​**Qutubuddin Aibak was the founder of the Ghulam Dynasty or Slave Dynasty in India, ruling from 1206 to 1210 AD.
 
• He started his career as a slave of Muhammad Ghori who later appointed him as the general.
 
• He is known for starting the construction of Qutub Minar, one of the historical monuments in Delhi, though it was completed by his successor, Iltutmish.
 
• Qutubuddin died in a polo accident in Lahore in 1210.
 
 
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni:**
 
 
• ​Mahmud of Ghazni was a Persianate Muslim who invaded the Indian subcontinent 17 times, most notably in 1025 when he attacked and plundered the Somnath Temple in the 11th century.
 
• His invasion of Somnath resulted in the destruction of the Jyotirlinga of the temple.
 
• He was also known for his punitive invasion of Anhilwara that followed the conquest of Somnath.
 
• Despite the destruction, there are records of pilgrimages to the temple in 1038 that do not mention any damage, suggesting potential repairs or rebuilds during this period.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Bin Qasim:**
 
 
• ​Muhammad Bin Qasim was an Umayyad general who, at the age of 17, began the first Muslim conquest of the Indian subcontinent in the 8th century.
 
• He conquered Sindh and Multan which became the easternmost province of the Umayyad Caliphate.
 
• Qasim is known for his fair administration, which provided a level of stability in the areas he conquered.
 
• He was recalled to Damascus after a political revolt and thereafter completely disappeared from historical records, with his ultimate fate uncertain.

questions.question: To which of the following gharanas of music did Ustad Amir Khan, a renowned vocalist, belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Indore__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Amir Khan** belongs to the** Indore Gharana** of music.
 
• He is one of the most influential Indian** vocalists** in the **Hindustani classical tradition** and is also known as **"Sur Rang"**.
 
• Ustad Amir Khan in fact is the** founder of the Indore Gharana,** a unique style of singing that **combined elements** of the **Kirana and Bhendibazaar Gharana**.
 
• His style is characterized by the amalgamation of multiple influences such as **Abdul Waheed Khan (vilambit tempo), Rajab Ali Khan (taans), **and **Aman Ali Khan (merukhand)**, resulting in an engaging blend of the spiritual flavor and grandeur of dhrupad with the ornate vividness of khayal.
 
• His impactful musical vision has resonated with and influenced a generation of musicians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agra Gharana:**

 
 
• The Agra gharana's style is known for its **deep meditative and spiritual approach** and for its systematic method of developing a raga.
 
• It includes **Nom-Tom alaaps** and **bold and forceful character of rendition** which are influences from the **Dhrupad style**.
 
• The Agra Gharana is unique in the treatment of rhythm where they use a variety of complex patterned layakari.
 
 
 
• **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana:**
 
 
• The Jaipur-Atrauli gharana evolved from **Dagar-bani of Dhrupad **and also absorbed finer essence of **Gauhar-bani and Khandar-bani**.
 
• It has a **systematic method of voice production**, which originates from the **Veena style of playing**.
 
 
 
• **Rangeela Gharana:**
 
 
• Rangeela Gharana is a** traditional school of music and dance** in India.
 
• The Gharana is known for its **emphasis on improvisation and creativity in music and dance**.
 
• Rangeela Gharana performances are characterized by their** lively and colorful costumes** and** expressive movements**.
 
• It has a strong emphasis on** rhythm** and** percussion instruments** in its music and dance compositions.
 
 
 
• **Indore Gharana:**
 
 
• **​**The founder of the Indore Gharana is **Ustad Amir Khan **who is known for his unique style revolving around a** slow tempo **and **meditative approach**.
 
• The gharana is characterized by **long expanses of sound **that are spread over **three octaves** and are sung in a deep meditative style.
 
• The gharana has a unique style o**f taans **which includes a** fast tempo done in a slow movement**.
 
• Ustad Amir Khan’s Indore gharana combines the** spiritual flavor of dhrupad **with the **ornate vividness of the khayal**.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts is regarded as the precursor to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Government Of India Act 1935__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The 1935 Government of India Act was a piece of legislation modified by the British Parliament. It was first given royal approval in August 1935.
 
• It called for the creation of an All-India federation with units made up of provinces and princely states. Three lists—the federal list, the provincial list, and the concurrent list—were used to distribute the powers between the center and the units.
 
• It did away with dyarchy in the provinces and replaced it with "provincial autonomy**"**.
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, having 321 sections and 10 schedules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Government of India Act 1935__

 __
 
• It was an Act adapted from the Parliament of the United Kingdom that received royal assent in August 1935.
 
• It had two main parts, dealing with the Federation of India and Provincial Autonomy.
 
• It provided for the establishment of a ‘Federation of India‘ consisting of the Governor’s Provinces and the Princely States.
 
• It withdrew dyarchy from the Provinces and implanted it at the Centre.
 
• It proposed a bicameral Federal Legislature with a Council of States and a Federal Assembly.
 
• It made a threefold division of subjects into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent.
 
• It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court with jurisdiction over the States and the Provinces.
 
• It separated Burma from India and gave Sind and North West Frontier Provinces the status of provinces.
 
• It introduced provincial autonomy by replacing provincial dyarchy with responsible government.
 
• It extended the principle of communal representation by providing separate electorates for depressed classes (scheduled castes), women and labour (workers).
 
 
 
• 
 
**Government of India Act of 1909 **__

 __
 
• The act was formulated by John Morley, secretary of state for India (1905–10).
 
• Lord Minto was the then Viceroy of India at that time.
 
• It considerably increased the size of the legislative councils, both Central and provincial.
 
• It retained an official majority in the Central Legislative Council but allowed the provincial legislative councils to have a non-official majority.
 
• It provided for the first time for the association of Indians with the executive councils of the Viceroy and Governors.
 
• It introduced a system of communal representation for Muslims by accepting the concept of a separate electorate.
 
• Some constituencies were earmarked for Muslims and only Muslims could vote their representatives.
 
 
 
• 
 
Government of India Act of 1919: __

 
 
• It was the codified version of the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms – named after Edwin Charles Montague and Lord Chelmsford. 
 
• It demarcated and separated the central and provincial subjects.
 
• It introduced dyarchy by dividing the provincial subjects into two parts—transferred and reserved.
 
• It introduced, for the first time, bicameralism in the central legislature and direct elections in the country.

questions.question: The boundary line separating one drainage basin from another is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Watershed__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **watershed **is also commonly referred to as a **drainage basin**.
 
• A** watershed or drainage basin** is an area of land where all the water that falls within it, whether through rainfall or other sources, drains into a common outlet such as a river, lake, or ocean.
 
• It is a** natural topographic boundary that defines the area from which water flows downhill and converges into a single point**.
 
• The term "**drain**" refers to a **channel or pipe** used to **remove excess water, while a pond is a small body of water typically formed by damming or artificially creating a depression**.
 
• Although** a river is often part of a watershed**, a watershed refers to the entire land area that contributes to the flow of water into that river, including the surrounding hills, valleys, and tributaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Watersheds: They are classified depending on the size, drainage, shape, and land use pattern.

 
 
• Macro watershed (> 50,000 Ha)
 
• Sub-watershed (10,000 to 50,000 Ha)
 
• Milli-watershed (1000 to 10,000 Ha)
 
• Micro watershed (100 to 1000 Ha)
 
• Mini watershed (1-100 Ha)
 
 
 
• **Peneplain**
 
 
• It is the end product of the fluvial cycle of erosion in the Davisian cycle of erosion.
 
• At the end of the third stage, the relief is almost destroyed and the land surface appears as a flat featureless plain known as ‘peneplain’.
 
• The peneplain may have in its fold a few hills which have still not lost their existence despite wasting.
 
• Davis called these isolated hills as ‘Monadnocks’
 
 
 
• Floodplain
 
 
• Floodplains are generally **flat areas of land that lie next to a river or stream**, extending from the river banks to the outer edges of the valley.
 
• They comprise two parts: the main channel of the river, called a **floodway**; and the **flood fringe**, which is the area that floods occasionally.
 
• **Floodways **can sometimes be seasonal, meaning the channel is dry for part of the year.
 
• **Floodplains **are susceptible to flooding because of their low-lying topography near rivers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://thewatershedproject.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/02/watershed_schematic.jpg]

questions.question: How are resources divided on the basis of status of development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential, developed, stock, and reserves.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resource refers to all the materials available in our environment that help us to satisfy our needs and wants.
 
• Resources are classified on the basis of their status of development which includes potential, developed stock, and reserves.
 
• Resources can be classified in the following ways–
 
 
• On the basis of origin – biotic and abiotic
 
• On the basis of exhaustibility – renewable and non-renewable
 
• On the basis of ownership – individual, community, national and international
 
• On the basis of the status of development – potential, developed, stock, and reserves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On the basis of the **status of development, resources are classified into four groups**, namely **potential**, **developed**, **stock**, and **reserve**.

 
 
• **Potential Resources**: Potential resources are those which are found in a region, but have not been utilized. For example, solar energy and wind energy, available in Rajasthan and Gujarat, have not been developed properly.
 
• **Developed Resources**: Developed resources are those that are estimated in terms of their quantity and quality for utilization, e.g., water, soil, and forests.
 
• **Stock Resources**: Materials in the environment that have the potential to satisfy human needs but are not technologically accessible to human beings, e.g., the use of water as a rich source of energy.
 
• **Reserve Resources**: A Reserve is a part of the stock that can be put to use in the near future with the help of existing technology, e.g., water in dams, and forests.

questions.question: Which of the following is an intermediate goods industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manufacturing of tools**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An intermediate good** is an incomplete good that goes as input for further finishing.
 
• Thus, in the production chain, Intermediate goods lie between raw materials and finished goods.
 
• The goods that don't need any more processing are referred to as final goods. These products, usually referred to as consumer goods, are created with the intention of being consumed directly by the final user. The goods that companies utilize to produce goods or services are referred to as intermediate goods.
 
• Since salt is used by producers to create other food products as well as directly consumed by customers, intermediate goods like salt can also be finished goods.
 
• A consumer good, also known as a final good or finished product, is made from an **intermediate item**.
 
• The following are examples of final goods: Items purchased by households are intended for consumption in their whole. For instance, television, milk, prepared meals, medications, and more. It also includes the products that businesses buy to raise funds or for investment purposes.
 
• Hence, the Manufacturing of tools is an example of an intermediate good.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Giffen Goods:

 
 
• A Giffen good is an inferior good with no close substitute available.
 
• Hypothetical example Bread is a good food source for people and when its price increases the people are forced to cut out other eatables like meat and spend more on bread. Hence its demand increases with price.
 
 
 
• Veblen Goods:
 
 
• When the price of goods rises, demand rises as well, and vice versa.
 
• Diamonds, for example, are luxury items whose attraction is based on their high price.
 
• It is named after Thorstein Veblen, an American economist.
 
 
 
• Convenience Goods:
 
 
• Convenience goods are items that are purchased frequently, quickly, and with minimal effort.
 
• These include candy, ice cream, cold drinks, cigarettes, magazines, and medicines, among other things.
 
 
 
• Public Goods:
 
 
• Goods with non-rivalry and non-excludability characteristics, such as national defense are known as public goods.
 
• A public good is a term in economics that refers to the good (commodity) that is available for use for everybody and one person’s usage of it does not diminish or exhaust its availability to others.
 
• Examples of public goods are education, infrastructure, lighthouses, flood control systems, knowledge, fresh air, national security, official statistics, etc.

__
 
• According to the **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022,** around **415 million** people in India climbed out of poverty between 2005-06 and 2019- 21.
 
• The recently released 2022 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** presents significant insights into global poverty dynamics.
 
• **Global Data**:Approximately 1.2 billion individuals are identified as multidimensionally poor, with almost half of them experiencing severe poverty.
 
 
• Among the impoverished, 593 million are children below the age of 18.Sub-Saharan Africa hosts the highest number of poor individuals (579 million), followed by South Asia (385 million), collectively representing 83% of the global impoverished population.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Pandemic**:The MPI data does not capture post-pandemic changes, but the report warns that the COVID-19 pandemic may reverse global poverty reduction progress by 3-10 years.
 
 
• According to the World Food Programme, the number of people in food crises or worse increased to 193 million in 2021.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Key Findings about India:

 
 
• India has the largest global population living in poverty, totaling 228 million, followed by Nigeria with 96 million.
 
• Two-thirds of the impoverished in India reside in households where at least one person faces nutritional deprivation.From 2005/06 to 2019/21, India witnessed a substantial reduction in poverty, with the incidence falling from 55.1% to 16.4%. 
 
• The improvements across all 10 MPI indicators contributed to more than halving the MPI value and poverty incidence.
 
• During the 15-year period from 2005-06 to 2019-21, 415 million people in India moved out of poverty, significantly influencing the decline in poverty in South Asia.South Asia now has a lower number of poor people compared to Sub-Saharan Africa.
 
 
 
• **Relative Reduction in Poverty : **
 
 
• The relative reduction in poverty accelerated from 2015/16 to 2019/21, with a rate of 11.9% per year, compared to 8.1% from 2005/06 to 2015/16.
 
• Bihar, the poorest state in 2015-16, exhibited the fastest reduction in MPI value in absolute terms.
 
 
 
• **Performances of States :**
 
 
• Bihar demonstrated substantial progress, with the percentage of poor decreasing from 77.4% in 2005-06 to 34.7% in 2019-21.
 
• While Bihar improved, most of the 10 poorest states in 2015/2016, except West Bengal, remained in the list in 2019-21.
 
 
 
• **Poverty among Children :**
 
 
• Absolute reduction in poverty among children was faster, despite India still having the highest number of poor children globally.
 
• More than one in five children in India live in poverty, compared to approximately one in seven adults.
 
 
 
• **Reduction of Poverty region wise :** 
 
 
• The incidence of poverty declined from 36.6% in 2015-2016 to 21.2% in 2019-2021 in rural areas and from 9.0% to 5.5% in urban areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a homeothermic animal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Penguin.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homeothermic animal** is one that can maintain a relatively constant internal body temperature regardless of external temperature fluctuations. 
 
• **Penguins** are an example of homeothermic animals.
 
• Penguins are birds and, like most birds and mammals, are endothermic or warm-blooded. 
 
• Penguins can generate and regulate their body heat internally. Penguins have specialized adaptations to survive in cold environments, such as a layer of insulating feathers and a thick layer of blubber. Despite living in extremely cold conditions, penguins maintain a stable internal body temperature.
 
• Salamander: Salamanders are ectothermic animals. They cannot internally regulate their body temperature and rely on external sources, such as the environment, to control their body temperature.
 
• Cobra: Cobras are reptiles and, like other reptiles, are ectothermic. They need external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature and cannot maintain a constant internal temperature.
 
• Tortoise: Tortoises are also reptiles and ectothermic. They depend on the external environment for temperature regulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ectothermic Animals: These animals, including reptiles and amphibians, rely on external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature. 

 
 
• They are often referred to as cold-blooded, but this doesn't mean their blood is cold; rather, their internal temperature varies with the environment.
 
 
 
• Endothermic Animals: These animals, such as mammals and birds, can generate and regulate their body heat internally. 
 
 
• They are often referred to as warm-blooded because they can maintain a relatively constant internal temperature, independent of external conditions. 
 
• Homeothermic animals are a subset of endothermic animals that actively maintain a stable internal body temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following factors are responsible for spoilage of stored food?

options.text: Low temperature and very high pressure
Moisture and humidity that can allow microbial growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **spoilage of stored food** is often influenced by various factors, and among the given options, the presence of moisture and humidity that allows microbial growth is a significant cause of food spoilage.
 
• Microorganisms, such as bacteria, molds, and yeast, thrive in environments with high moisture content.
 
• Moisture provides a conducive environment for microbial growth, leading to the spoilage of food. This can result in the development of off-flavors, odors, and visible signs of decay.
 
• **Low Temperature and Very High Pressure**: Low temperature is generally associated with preserving food rather than causing spoilage.
 
 
• Cold temperatures slow down the growth of microorganisms and can extend the shelf life of certain foods. Very high pressure is not a common factor in the spoilage of stored food.
 
 
 
• **High Temperature and Pressure**: High temperature can accelerate the growth of microorganisms and enzymatic reactions, leading to food spoilage.
 
 
• High pressure is not typically a factor in the spoilage of stored food but is sometimes used in food processing to extend shelf life.
 
 
 
• **High Salt and Spice Content**: High salt content acts as a preservative by drawing out moisture and inhibiting microbial growth.
 
 
• However, extremely high salt levels can affect the taste and texture of food. High spice content, in moderation, is not typically a cause of spoilage but may impact the flavor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Factors Contributing to Food Spoilage**:

 
 
• ​**Oxygen Exposure:** Exposure to oxygen can lead to oxidative reactions, causing rancidity and spoilage, particularly in fats and oils.
 
• **Inadequate Packaging**: Improper packaging that allows the entry of air, moisture, or pests can contribute to food spoilage.
 
• **Enzymatic Activity: **Enzymes naturally present in food can become active, leading to changes in color, flavor, and texture.
 
• **Contamination:** Introduction of pathogens or spoilage microorganisms during processing, handling, or storage can cause food spoilage.

questions.question: Which of the following factors is a geographical factor that affects the distribution of the population in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Climate.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Geographical factors play a crucial role in influencing the distribution of the population, and among the options provided, **climate **is a significant geographical factor that affects population distribution.
 
• Climate : The climate of a region, including factors such as temperature, precipitation, and humidity, directly impacts the suitability of an area for human habitation. 
 
 
• People are more likely to settle in areas with a climate that is conducive to their lifestyle and livelihoods. 
 
• For example, regions with moderate temperatures, ample rainfall, and fertile soil are often more attractive for settlement.
 
 
 
• Industrialization: While industrialization can influence population distribution by creating job opportunities in urban areas, it is not a geographical factor in the same way that climate is. 
 
 
• Industrialization often leads to the growth of urban centers, which, in turn, attracts people from rural areas.
 
 
 
• Minerals: The presence of minerals can influence economic activities and, consequently, population distribution. 
 
 
• However, this is more related to economic factors than pure geography. Areas rich in minerals may experience population growth due to mining activities and related industries.
 
 
 
• Urbanization: Urbanization is a process where people move from rural areas to urban centers. It is a result of various factors, including industrialization and economic opportunities. 
 
 
• While urbanization influences where people live, it is more of a social and economic process than a geographical factor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other Geographical Factors:

 
 
• ​Topography: The physical features of the land, such as mountains, plains, and rivers, can influence settlement patterns and the distribution of the population.
 
• Soil Fertility: Fertile soil is essential for agriculture, and regions with fertile soil are often more densely populated due to the availability of agricultural resources.
 
• Water Sources: Proximity to water bodies, such as rivers, lakes, and oceans, can affect population distribution as water is crucial for human survival and economic activities.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the zones of a pond ecosystem from the bottom to top?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Option 1__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct sequence of the zones of a pond ecosystem from the bottom to top is **Hypolimnion-Thermocline-Epilimnion.**
 
• Hypolimnion: The hypolimnion is the bottom layer of a pond or lake. It is characterized by lower temperatures and typically has minimal mixing with the upper layers. 
 
 
• This zone often contains colder, denser water and is less influenced by surface temperature changes.
 
 
 
• Thermocline: The thermocline is the middle layer where a rapid temperature change occurs. It acts as a barrier between the warmer upper layer (epilimnion) and the colder lower layer (hypolimnion). 
 
 
• The thermocline is a region where temperature decreases rapidly with depth.
 
 
 
• Littoral: The littoral zone is the top layer of a pond or lake, extending from the shoreline to the open water area. 
 
 
• It is the shallow, nearshore region where sunlight penetrates to the bottom, supporting the growth of aquatic plants. 
 
• This zone is often rich in biodiversity and provides important habitat for various organisms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A pond ecosystem consists of various zones, each characterized by different environmental conditions and supporting distinct communities of organisms. 
 
• The main zones of a pond ecosystem, from the bottom to the top, are as follows:
 
 
• 
 
Benthic Zone:

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The benthic zone is the bottom layer of the pond, comprising the sediment and substrate. It can include mud, sand, rocks, and organic matter.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: Benthic organisms include various bottom-dwelling invertebrates such as worms, insect larvae, and crustaceans. Some fish species may also forage in this zone.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
​Hypolimnion: 

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The hypolimnion is the deep, colder layer of the pond located below the thermocline. It remains thermally stratified and less affected by surface temperature changes.

 
 
• 
 
Temperature: The temperature in the hypolimnion is relatively constant and lower than in the epilimnion.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: Some cold-water fish species and deep-water invertebrates may inhabit this zone.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Thermocline:

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The thermocline is a transitional layer between the warmer upper layer (epilimnion) and the colder lower layer (hypolimnion). It is characterized by a rapid temperature change with depth.

 
 
• 
 
Temperature: The temperature decreases quickly with depth in the thermocline.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: The thermocline may influence the distribution of plankton and fish, as it marks a temperature transition.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Epilimnion:

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The epilimnion is the upper layer of the pond, extending from the surface to the thermocline. It is influenced by sunlight and mixing due to wind, leading to relatively uniform temperatures.

 
 
• 
 
Temperature: The temperature is warmer in the epilimnion, and sunlight penetration supports photosynthesis.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: This zone supports a variety of phytoplankton, aquatic plants, and fish species. It is often rich in biodiversity.

 
 
 
 
• **Littoral Zone**:
 
 
• **​Description**: The littoral zone is the shallow, nearshore area of the pond where light penetrates to the bottom. It includes the area from the shoreline to the point where rooted plants no longer grow.
 
• **Organisms**: The littoral zone supports a diverse range of aquatic plants, algae, and a variety of invertebrates. It is an important habitat for amphibians, insects, and smaller fish.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India (2022-23), which fiber crop is the major producer in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Telangana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Cotton__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Ministry of Textile, Government of India (2022-23), Cotton is majorly produced in **Gujarat, Maharashtra and Telangana**.
 
• Cotton holds immense significance in India, being one of the primary commercial crops and contributing approximately **25% to the global cotton production**. 
 
• It plays a pivotal role in supporting the livelihoods of around 6 million cotton farmers and engaging 40-50 million people in related activities like cotton processing and trade. 
 
• The Indian Textile Industry is a major consumer of various fibers and yarns, with a usage ratio of around 60:40 for cotton to non-cotton fibers, deviating from the global ratio of 30:70.
 
• Apart from meeting the fundamental need for clothing, cotton significantly contributes to India's net foreign exchange through exports. Often referred to as "**White-Gold**," it is a major export commodity, with raw cotton, yarn, fabric, garments, made-ups, and knitwear being sent to global markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Acreage under Cotton and Yield:

 
 
• ​India leads the world in cotton acreage, covering 120.69 lakh hectares, which accounts for around 36% of the global cotton cultivation area.
 
• Around 67% of India's cotton is grown in rain-fed areas, while 33% is in irrigated areas.
 
• India ranks 38th in productivity with a yield of 510 kg/ha.
 
 
 
• Production and Consumption of Cotton:
 
 
• ​India is a **major producer** of all four species of cultivated cotton.
 
• Ten major cotton-growing states are grouped into three agro-ecological zones: Northern, Central, and Southern.
 
• India ranks **first globally in cotton production**, contributing 23% of the world's production.
 
• India is the **second-largest consumer of cotton**, using 22% of the world's cotton consumption.
 
 
 
• Import and Export of Cotton:
 
 
• ​India is the **third-largest exporter** of cotton, accounting for 8% of the world's export.
 
• India imports less than 10% of its total cotton consumption to meet specific requirements of the textile industry.
 
 
 
• International Scenario:
 
 
• ​Global cotton production for 2021/22 is forecasted to increase by 9% from the previous season, with consumption estimated at 25.6 million tonnes.
